messages.subject: Structural change in *TAR models
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Mat!
     As I told you, there is a new pair of eyes and hands looking into
the codes of tsDyn. Christoph Bergmeir, who is in CC in this message,
has been reading the part of the code which deals with the STAR and
NCSTAR models. He has some good ideas for a change of internal
representation of some models, and I'm inviting him to propose them to
you. He is also considering some parallelization alternatives.
     He will need to have access to the repositories, and I'm going to
look into this. However, looking at the Google Code repository, it is
not stated there that we have moved to GIT, it might be important to
write that down to prevent people from downloading the outdated code
shown there. What do you think?

messages.subject: Re: Structural change in *TAR models
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone!

> I am glad you will be helping and contributing to tsDyn... great!
> Indeed, Jose did a nice work with this ncstar and I was always sad it is
> not used :-) So I will be happy to hear about your ideas for the starr
> and ncstar() functions! Note that I am working presently on Markov
> models, so we might at some time end up with a quite complete package!

So, yes, the idea was to polish the ncstar things up a little so that they can be made public, and within that we also wanted to do the changes necessary for us to use the tsDyn package in the way we'd like to.

So, I'll explain the changes I have in mind a little:

Each model (star, setar, ncstar ,...) initially creates its own nlar.struct object. The nlar.struct saves an embedded version of the series, so that the *TAR models later are used internally like any other generic regression model, i.e. with a matrix of data input and a vector of data output.

Well, I'm not sure whether it actually makes sense to use the *TAR models for regression, let's say with including exogeneous variables in the input and so forth, but that each model generates its nlar.struct makes the code quite inflexible, especially because it is not possible to specify exactly in the embedd of tseriesChaos (which is used internally by nlar.struct) the lags to use:
For example, as far as I'm familiar with the package, only one-step-ahead predictions are directly supported, right? (the function to make predictions with the models is called "oneStep (...)") However, with another embedding it would be very easy to choose any lag as forecast horizon.

Also, with respect to the nnetTS model of the tsDyn package the advantages of a more generic interface are quite obvious: Instead of making it necessary to write a wrapper for each regression function (in this case nnet), I think it would be better just to use the same interface as nnet, and to separate the preprocessing. So, what I have in mind is something like:

# Use lags -2, -4, -5, so it's two-step-ahead
embeddedTS <- embed(c (-2, -4, -5), ts)
myModel <- nnet (embeddedTS$values, embeddedTS$targets, ...)  #here goes any model, i.e. also ncstar, star, setar,...
# Values is a matrix with 3 columns (one per lag). targets is a vector of the values lag0
predictions <- predict (myModel, newData)

I already implemented a function that does embedding like this (i.e. with taking a list of exactly which lags to use)..

To implement these changes actually there is not so much to do. The easiest way would be to add just an additional parameter of type nlar.struct in each model. If it is present, then this nlar.struct is taken and the model doesn't generate one on it's own. The rest could be done with convenience functions calling that function..

As soon as I find the time I'll have a look into Git and probably I'll implement all the changes I have in mind..as far as I understand Git, "everything is a branch", so that it should be quite easy to later put things together.. Actually, what has happened is the following: About 3 weeks ago, I planned to work with highest priority on tsDyn. But then I began implementing some things on my own into a new package, so that I'd like to put some more work into that first (maybe a week or so).. This has the advantage that I'm currently getting familiar with all the R packaging stuff first, which probably is necessary..

By the way: How is the documentationof tsDyn generated?..a week ago I had a look into Roxygen  (it's on CRAN), and I really like it..

Cheers,
Christoph

So you would like to include external variable? For which type of model?
With simultaneous values, or only lagged one? Like a *TAR ARDL? Or say
simply cross section regression with one variable having *TAR impact on
the left-side one?

I think both would make sense. For the first, a *TAR ARDL, this should
maybe be directly done in a more general VAR way. We have now VAR and
TVAR (threshold VAR), maybe STTVAR would be interesting?

On the other side, *TAR cross regression would be also interesting! In
this case, there would be the question whether one needs a t all to use
the nlar.struc...

Concerning your point on embed and different lags... note that now is
setar()  there is a kind of parallel implementation, with MH which can
be lags c(1,3,7), is this what you mean? To do this, I don't think a
change of the nlar.stru is necessary, just selecting after the lags
should be enough, no?

I am not quite sure to follow you on the issue of forecast horizonts and
number of lags... you feel it can't be extended to larger horiztons
without this lag issue?

messages.subject: Re: tsDyn: Bugs and suggestions of improvements
messages.subject_clean: tsDyn: Bugs and suggestions of improvements
messages.body_plain:
Dear Mr Larsen

Thanks a lot for bug report and detailed comments. incidentally, I have been working last week on some of those points, which have been partly corrected. It is more a workaround, and I plan to deal with it more deeply in the few weeks/months. I'll be happy to send you the corrected dev version if you are keen on giving it a test.

Cocnerning point 4, this is not a limitation of the package but the literature. Because we do a grid search, estimating more than 2-3 parameters is almost unfeasible. There are nevertheless alternatives, with genetic algorithms, or by smoothing the indicator function (so using conventional optim methods). I feel those are the areas where your inputs could be most valuable! And we would welcome a lot your contribution in this domain! I attach two papers to give overview of those methods.

Best
Matthieu Stigler

PS: ccing to our mailing-list, to which you are welcome to subscribe.

Le 21. 10. 10 11:12, Berner Larsen a écrit :
>
> To the maintainer of the package tsDyn!
>
>
>
> I am trying to model time series of Norwegian interest rates by using the TVECM function in the tsDyn package. However, I get the following error messages and warnings when I use TVECM on my data (the R script and the data file are attached):
>
> 1.       “Error in if (min(n1, n2, 1 - n1 - n2) > trim) { :          missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed. “  I think the reason is that a test whether n2 is available should be included in the functions two_partial_Thresh and two_thresh in the source code file TVECM.R
>
> 2.       When I insert the statement    if(is.na <http://is.na>(n2)==TRUE) {n1<-0; n2<-0} just after the statement    if(is.na <http://is.na>(n1)==TRUE) {n1<-0; n2<-0}   in the functions two_partial_Thresh and two_thresh, and rerun my test script, I get the following error message: “Error in if (positionSecond <= length(storeMinus)) { :   missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed     In addition:  Warning message:  In min(store2, na.rm = TRUE) :  no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf”.   I think the problem here is that both storePlus and storeMinus is NA. Are the if-tests used when computing storeMinus and storePlus correct? [copy from TVECM.R: ” if(wh.thresh>2*ninter){ “   and   “if(length(wh.thresh<length(allgammas)-2*ninter)){ “. I do not understand the condition in the last of these if-tests.]
>
> 3.       In the function print.summary.TVECM I think that a “\n”, should be inserted at the end of the statement cat("\nPercentage of Observations in each regime", percent(x$model.specific$nobs,digits=3,by100=TRUE))      to secure that the summary command is properly finished. I am using ESS and GNU Emacs and the script is hanging when I try to execute the summary command. (As TVECM fails when ntresh=2, I set nthresh=1 in this case.) But if I replace the statement above with “cat("\nPercentage of Observations in each regime", percent(x$model.specific$nobs,digits=3,by100=TRUE),”\n”) the script runs successfully. I know that ESS searches for the R prompt “>” to terminate a script, so when the print function is not properly finished by a return, ESS is waiting for the R prompt which does not come. Consequently, ESS is hanging. It is not a large problem, as I may terminate the script with C-g.
>
> 4.       If I try to use TVECM with a data set of 3 variables, I get the message “Sorry, the search is only possible with 2 variables. If more, please provide pre-specified beta values”. It would have been nice to extend TVECM to the 3 variable case.
>
>
>
> I am an associate professor in mathematics and statistics at Bodø Graduate School of Business in Norway. I have a Phd in mathematics from 1998 at University of Tromsø in Norway. The title of the dissertation is “Searching for polynomials in the number field sieve”, and I used the freeware PARI/GP which is a computer algebra system designed for fast computations in number theory, originally developed by Henri Cohen and his co-workers at University of Bordeaux. I wrote my own C programs which called the number theoretic functions from the PARI library.  Now, I am teaching mathematics and statistics , and I am cooperating with colleagues in finance and transport economics on writing articles.  I have used R the last three years by making short scripts to do simulations, explore data sets and make plots. As a part-time work, I am enrolled as a student on a Master Degree Program in Statistics at University of Tromsø (in Norway). My plan is to let time series modeling by using threshold cointegration be the main theme in my Master thesis.  Therefore, I am interested in cooperating with you on correcting bugs and implementing added functionality as point 4. above. Do not hesitate to get in touch with me if you are interested in my cooperation on developing parts of the package tsDyn.
>
>
>
> Yours sincerely,
>
>
>
> Berner Larsen
>
> Bodø Graduate School of Business
>
> N-8049 Bodø
>
> Norway
